A task the maintainer set by ruling: batch #382 item 1 on #24932, Q1 **C** (decision 6318800595, 「同意」), filed by the director seat. First in the pick order: a maintainer-ruled card outranks the label order. #24932 (`domain:services`, p1) merges after this card.
Session: `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy` (the dispatching seat; the dev runs as its own cloud session, named in the dispatch comment)
Account: `os-project-manager` (the seat's linked user as `GET /user` answers it; always the card's assignee)
Branch: `claude/issue-25144-controlled-by-parent-unservable-master-refused`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-25144`
Domain: `domain:engine`
Seat: `domain:engine#1` (seat post #6367)
File surface:
- **Measured first, the ruled confidence gap:** where the boot can see both facts.
  - **Middleware:** every object-scoped read middleware a plugin registers in `start()` (`registerMiddleware(fn, { object })`). The card enumerates comment, activity, the audit ledger, mail, attachment, position assignment and approval request.
  - **Bindings:** every object's datasource binding (`resolveDatasourceBinding`).
  - **The candidates:** a `kernel:ready` hook in the engine (`packages/objectql`), or `registerApp` if both facts are already resolvable there.
  - Measure which point sees a middleware registered later in plugin start. ⛔ A check that cannot see a registration made after it runs is not the refusal asked for.
  - If neither engine point sees both facts and only `packages/runtime` (`domain:cli`) does, report `needs_decision` instead of building there.
- **The refusal, in `packages/objectql` at the measured point:** a `controlled_by_parent` detail whose master (a) resolves to a datasource other than the detail's, or (b) carries an object-scoped read middleware, refuses the boot.
  - It is loud, the way ADR-0139 D3's envelope is. It names the detail, the master, the class and the remedy: bind both to one datasource; choose a master without an object-scoped read middleware; or declare the detail without `controlled_by_parent`.
  - Reuse the read-time predicates the engine already uses (`hasObjectMiddleware`, `resolveDatasourceBinding`, `engine.ts` near `:6546`–`:6557`), so the boot rule and the read rule cannot drift.
  - ⛔ No silent skip, and no fallback to an id list.
- **Pins:** one per class, (a) and (b), on the production boot path, plus a mastered-by-`sys_attachment` case. Controls: HotCRM's six `controlled_by_parent` objects (the card's `e6d5d3e` reading), the showcase and every in-repo example boot unchanged. Ablation: remove the refusal, and both class pins go red while the controls stay green.
- **The changeset:** BREAKING, as AGENTS.md's changeset rule spells it for a narrowing. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` (the spec parse does not move; a spec shape moving would be a fork), the BREAKING banner, the migration (the three remedies) and its ADR-0087 disposition, at the level `check-changeset-no-major` takes for the packages moved.

⛔ Not in scope:
- `ObjectSchema.parse` and `packages/spec` (the ruling: deployment facts, not a spec parse);
- `os validate`, unless it already resolves bindings;
- #24932's plugin-security switch (`domain:services`'), #25092 and #25106;
- the read-time refusal itself (ADR-0139 D5.2 / D5.3 stay as they are).

Container & model: `M`, `mode:cloud` (a boot-time refusal at a measured point, two classes, controls and a dogfood battery), `model: TIER_DEFAULT` to build (this run's `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier`: "no path-derived mandate"). The review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, since a narrowing declaration is a contract face.
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Responsibility: an author who declares a `controlled_by_parent` detail over a master on another datasource, or over a master an object-scoped read middleware narrows | the declaration boots today and, once #24932's leaf lands, answers 500 for every caller at read | every stack carrying such a declaration (none measured in HotCRM or in-repo; deployed tenants unread)
Thread-read: none
Serial constraints cleared: the 12 open PRs' file lists were read at this claim, on `origin/main` `23540582f4`. None touches `packages/objectql/src`. #24932 develops in parallel and merges second, by the ruling.

  - pins for both classes (one mastered by `sys_attachment`), with HotCRM's six shapes, the showcase and every example as controls, plus an ablation;

- **Not built:** `ObjectSchema.parse` / `packages/spec`; #24932's switch (it merges after this); #25092; #25106.
- **Owed:** a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record before the queue, since this is a narrowing.

## Late-install measurement

Relayed by `domain:engine` seat 1 (`session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`) at 2026-10-22T04:23Z, verbatim from dev `session_01Dw4pQznF7eB7VtCsFQXMAH`. The dev's dispatch allowed three writes, and all three were spent, so the seat posts it. Nothing was pushed and PR #25166 is unchanged.

> Head `0f5d9a6bc` (PR #25166), detached worktree, one uncommitted scratch test `packages/objectql/src/zz-late-install-measure.test.ts`, deleted afterwards (`git status` clean, worktree removed). Command: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/objectql^...' build` (under the lock), then `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/zz-late-install-measure.test.ts` in `packages/objectql` (7/7 cases ran). Setup: a real `ObjectKernel` with `ObjectQLPlugin` and a host plugin that registers drivers `primary` (default) and `archive`. For class (b), the host also registers `registerMiddleware(fn, { object: MASTER })` from its own `kernel:ready`. Every kernel booted clean (no offender at boot). No `plugin-security` is in this kernel. A plain read therefore carries no leaf, so the leaf read writes `{ parent: { $in: ReadableIds.of(MASTER) } }` explicitly, as #24932's consumer will.
>
> - **Control:** the same class (a) package registered during boot is refused at `bootstrap()` with `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 ("A controlled_by_parent detail derives its access from a master the engine cannot compose a read over: 'ba_detail' (master field 'parent') over master 'ba_master', which is bound to datasource 'archive' while 'ba_detail' is bound to 'primary' (ADR-0139 D5.3). …").
> - **Step 1/2, `protocol.installPackage` (the method `POST /api/v1/packages` calls):** this door cannot carry an object definition. `ManifestSchema.objects` is `z.array(z.string())` (globs). An inline object is refused: "Invalid package manifest — manifest.objects.0: Invalid input: expected string, received object". With globs the install succeeds (`{ package, message }`) and registers no object (`getAllObjects('com.measure.late-g')` is `[]`); `registry.installPackage` records the package only. So no late CBP detail is reachable through the install door in a plain kernel. The steps fell back to the `manifest` service, the artifact-registration door marketplace installs use. My first run used underscore ids, which the install door correctly refused for the reverse-domain id; that run was discarded.
> - **Step 1, class (a), `manifest.register` after `bootstrap()` resolved:** resolves, and the detail and master register. Plain `find(detail)` answers 200 / 0 rows. Leaf `find(detail)` answers `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500, "find('ma_detail'): where.parent.$in holds a ReadableIds leaf, \"the ids of 'ma_master' this caller may read\", and the engine composes no such leaf over 'ma_master', which is bound to datasource 'archive' while 'ma_detail' is bound to 'primary': no driver evaluates a subquery across two datasources. The query was NOT run and no driver was asked. …". `findUnservableControlledByParentMasters()` lists it (`other-datasource`), so the predicate sees it; nothing asks it after boot.
> - **Step 2, class (b), `manifest.register` after boot (master gated at `kernel:ready`, `hasObjectMiddleware` true):** resolves, and the detail registers. Plain find answers 0 rows. Leaf find answers `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500, "… and the engine composes no such leaf over 'mb_master', whose rows an object-scoped read middleware narrows: that WHERE is built at read time and is no part of its read scope, so the composed leaf would be wider than a read of 'mb_master'. The query was NOT run …". `findUnservableControlledByParentMasters()` lists it (`object-scoped-read-middleware`).
> - **Step 3, `metadata:reloaded`:** reachable in-process. A plugin `ctx.trigger('metadata:reloaded', { metadata: { objects: [...] } })` (the payload shape `ingestReloadedObjects` reads) resolves without refusal, and the class (a) pair registers. Plain find answers 0 rows; leaf find answers the same `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 (D5.3) as step 1. The predicate lists it. Class (b) over reload was not run separately; it is the same ingest plus the step-2 predicate.
> - **Step 4, dedupe:** the REST search endpoint (`GET /search/issues`) answers 403 in this container (it is bound to repo-scoped endpoints). I used the repo-scoped MCP `search_issues` instead; it is semantic matching, not keyword. `controlled_by_parent late install`: 0 hits. `metadata:reloaded controlled_by_parent`: 0 hits. Control `controlled_by_parent`: 14 hits (#25144, #25095, #25044, #24962, #25049, …), so the zeros are not a dead search. No hit names a late-install or reload refusal. The nearest are #25144 itself, and #25092 (a write door, from the card).
>
> reach (for the filing gate): no public HTTP door was measured. The install door cannot carry definitions; the reachable doors are the in-process `manifest` service and `metadata:reloaded`. Both admit the declaration after boot, and the declaration answers 500 only on a leaf read. Today no production read writes that leaf; it will once #24932 lands.

**Seat's reading: no card today.**
- **No public entry was measured.** The filing gate wants `reach:` measured once through a public entry, or a named real producer. Here the HTTP install door cannot carry an object definition at all. The doors that admit a late detail are in-process: the `manifest` service and `metadata:reloaded`.
- **No production read writes the leaf yet.** The 500 needs a `ReadableIds` leaf, and no production read writes one today.
- **When to re-ask.** Once #24932 lands, its consumer writes that leaf. Then a late detail over an unservable master answers 500 on a read, where the boot rule would have refused it. At that point the seat re-measures reach through the marketplace install route, the producer named above, and files a card if it reaches. The card's shape would follow the picklist and bound-action precedent in `plugin.ts`: judge the detail on arrival once the boot has sealed.

**What `main` now holds:**
- **The boot refuses an unservable `controlled_by_parent` detail.** A detail whose one required master is bound to another datasource (ADR-0139 D5.3), or whose master an object-scoped read middleware narrows (D5.2), now stops the boot. The refusal is `INVALID_METADATA` / 422. It names each detail, master field, master and class, and the three remedies:
  - bind both to one datasource;
  - choose a master without an object-scoped read middleware;
  - drop `controlled_by_parent`.
  Before, such a deployment booted and answered 500 on the read that composed the leaf.
- **Where it runs.** `ObjectQLPlugin`'s `kernel:bootstrapped` handler, after every plugin's `kernel:ready` has registered its middleware and every binding is final, and before `kernel:listening` opens the socket.
- **One rule, two callers.** The read-time refusal and the boot rule ask one private predicate. The read-time messages are byte-identical to before. The predicate is reachable as `ObjectQL#findUnservableControlledByParentMasters()`.
- **Reach:** every deployment that boots `ObjectQLPlugin` with the boot-phase hooks. The in-repo `controlled_by_parent` details (app-crm and app-showcase) master on same-package, ungated objects and boot unchanged.
- **Shipped as:** `patch` of `@objectstack/objectql`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, with the BREAKING banner, the Remedy section and ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

**Beside it:**
- **Unblocked.** #24932 (`domain:services`, the leaf switch) is now unblocked per ruling 6329027469 ②. Its seat re-claims.
- **Not covered: late artifacts.** The boot rule covers the boot only. An artifact registered after boot is admitted, through the `manifest` service or `metadata:reloaded`, and refused at read with the engine's D5 500 (measurement 6332654314). The HTTP install door cannot carry an object definition. No card today, because no public entry was measured and no production read writes the leaf before #24932. The seat re-measures when #24932 lands.
- **Not filed:** the return type `UnservableControlledByParentMaster` is not re-exported from the package root (the record's ① item 2 nit).

The dev session `session_01Dw4pQznF7eB7VtCsFQXMAH` is archived.
